episodes.title: Mock Interview: Financial AI Assistant / AgentOS
episodes.description: LLM as untrusted planner, never the authorization layer. Tiered action model (Tier 0-3), deterministic policy engine, tool allowlists, server-generated payment intents with canonical summaries, prompt injection defense (6 layers), RAG for documentation, permissioned APIs for account data, step-up authentication for money movement, cross-tenant isolation at infrastructure level.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Webhook & Event Delivery Platform
episodes.description: Transactional outbox pattern for guaranteed event creation, at-least-once delivery with merchant deduplication, per-endpoint queues for tenant isolation, HMAC-signed payloads with timestamp, SSRF protection (DNS rebinding, private IP blocks, redirect limits), exponential backoff with jitter, event replay, and event-list API for recovery.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Bulk Payouts & Batch Payments
episodes.description: Million-row batch processing with streaming validation, deterministic item keys for idempotency, partner-sharded work queues with rate limits, lease-based worker claims, aggregate funding reservation, partial cancellation semantics, and downloadable results. All-or-nothing for validation/funding, independent per-item execution.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Bank & Partner Reconciliation
episodes.description: Reconciliation as a continuous control system, not a nightly report. Immutable evidence ingestion, multi-phase matching algorithm (exact reference then fuzzy candidates), aggregate balance control, exception case management, safe repairs via compensating journals. Zero tolerance for unexplained money differences.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Card Authorization & Issuing Platform
episodes.description: Authorization hold lifecycle, atomic check-and-reserve, deduplication by network transaction ID, clearing matching, partial clearing and incremental authorizations, disputes, stand-in mode with bounded offline limits, and card controls. 150ms SLA for real-time authorization decisions.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Multi-Currency Wallet & Double-Entry Ledger
episodes.description: Immutable double-entry journal as source of truth, balance projections for reads, atomic reserve/settle/release flows, optimistic concurrency with version checks, FX conversion with balanced legs per currency, rounding entries, and balance rebuild from journal replay. Covers the same fundamentals as Airwallex's core ledger system.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: KYC/Onboarding System
episodes.description: Multi-jurisdiction KYC, fuzzy name matching (double metaphone + Levenshtein), risk scoring, ongoing monitoring, GDPR pseudonymization, KYC GenAI for false positive reduction, 5-min auto-approval.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Idempotent API for Financial Operations
episodes.description: Client-generated idempotency keys, Redis for speed + PostgreSQL for truth, same-transaction atomicity, unique constraint dedup, saga step idempotency, background reaper for stale records.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Low-Latency FX Pricing System
episodes.description: WebSocket price streaming, sub-100ms end-to-end, best bid/ask aggregation across providers, backpressure throttling, indicative vs tradeable rates, rate audit trail for regulators.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Multi-Region Global Infrastructure
episodes.description: Active-active reads, leader-per-entity writes, synchronous replication, RPO <1min, RTO <5min, data sovereignty per jurisdiction, split-brain prevention, chaos engineering drills.

episodes.title: System Design Q&A — Power Answers
episodes.description: Deep Q&A covering the 12 Airwallex interview topics — 5 generic plus 7 domain-specific. For each: killer questions interviewers ask, structured answers that score, common mistakes that lose points, and cross-cutting patterns like RESHADED.

episodes.title: Back-of-Envelope Estimation Masterclass
episodes.description: Every number you need for system design interviews, organized around 12 real interview problems. Power numbers, latency defaults, throughput benchmarks, fintech-specific numbers, and how to derive any number from first principles when you forget.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Fraud Detection System
episodes.description: Design a fraud detection system with rule-based + ML ensemble scoring, real-time feature engineering (velocity, amount, location, behavioral), point-in-time correctness, and feedback loops for model improvement. Covers Airwallex's approach to global transaction monitoring with low false-positive rates.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Feature Store / ML Infrastructure
episodes.description: Design a feature store like Airwallex's AirSkiff: batch/streaming unification where the same feature logic works for both real-time and batch, point-in-time joins to prevent ML data leakage, low-latency online serving (2-150ms), and a feature registry for cross-team reuse. 100+ features, 10K TPS serving.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Global Treasury Network
episodes.description: Design a global treasury network for multi-entity cash management: notional pooling, zero-balancing sweeps, payment netting to reduce FX costs, inter-company settlements, and per-jurisdiction regulatory constraints. Covers the same challenges Airwallex faces connecting 50+ countries with capital controls.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Metrics & Monitoring Pipeline
episodes.description: Designing time-series storage, cardinality control, and SLO-driven alerting. Generic system design mock interview.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Job Scheduler
episodes.description: Designing reliable job scheduling with idempotency, retry, and failure handling. Generic system design mock interview.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Security Automation Platform
episodes.description: Design a security automation platform like the CVE lifecycle system: overnight AI diagnosis, morning dashboard with triaged findings, built-in discussion bot, one-click remediation. Covers SAST/DAST/SCA integration, transitive dependency scanning, and shadow-mode validation — matching Airwallex's security-first fintech requirements.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: AI Agent Platform (AgentOS)
episodes.description: Design Airwallex's AgentOS platform: plugin-based AI agents with sandboxed execution, natural-language intent parsing, real-time policy enforcement, and audit trails. Covers the SDD (Spec-Driven Development) pipeline where agents produce specs, users approve, and code is verified against the spec.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Wallet (Auticuro)
episodes.description: Design a distributed wallet using Airwallex's Auticuro architecture: single-threaded state machine with NO LOCKS, Raft consensus for strong consistency, RocksDB WriteBatch for atomic persistence, client-provided dedup_id for exactly-once semantics. P99 < 20ms at 10K TPS. CQRS with 4-thread design per node.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Ride Sharing (Uber)
episodes.description: Designing driver matching, surge pricing, and real-time location tracking. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Video Streaming (YouTube)
episodes.description: Designing video upload, transcoding, CDN delivery, and adaptive bitrate. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Rate Limiter
episodes.description: Designing API rate limiting with token bucket and distributed counters. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Key-Value Store
episodes.description: Designing a DynamoDB-like KV store with consistent hashing and quorum. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Web Crawler
episodes.description: Designing a scalable distributed web crawler with politeness and dedup. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

episodes.description: YouTube-extracted mock system design interview: designing India's UPI payment system with Gaurav Sen.

episodes.description: YouTube-extracted expert system design interview: designing Uber Eats with a senior Netflix engineer. Real interview walkthrough.

episodes.title: Design a Payment System — Expert Interview
episodes.description: YouTube-extracted expert system design interview: designing a payment system like Stripe. Real interview walkthrough with an experienced engineer.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Location-Based Service
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: designing nearby-driver search and real-time location tracking using geohash, quadtree, and S2 geometry. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Real-Time Chat
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a WhatsApp-like messaging system with WebSocket delivery, read receipts, and group chat fan-out. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Top-K / Heavy Hitters
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: finding the most frequent items in a data stream at scale using Count-Min Sketch, heaps, and sliding window algorithms. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: FX & Multi-Currency Ledger
episodes.description: Design an FX rate engine with provider aggregation, rate locking with TTL, and a per-currency double-entry ledger with three-entry cross-currency transfers. Covers the same fundamentals as Airwallex's real-time FX engine serving 130+ currency pairs.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Object Storage (S3)
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a durable object storage system with erasure coding, multipart upload, and 11-nines durability. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Typeahead / Search Autocomplete
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a sub-50ms autocomplete system using tries, pre-computed suggestions, and Lambda architecture for freshness. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Notification System
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a multi-channel notification system supporting push, email, and SMS with templates, preferences, and delivery tracking. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Cache
episodes.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a Redis-like distributed caching system with consistent hashing, virtual nodes, replication, and rebalancing. Two-voice dialogue.

episodes.title: Mock Interview: Cross-Border Payments
episodes.description: Design a cross-border payment pipeline with FX conversion, idempotency keys, compliance screening, and bank connector adapters. Covers the full saga pattern with compensating actions — the same architecture Airwallex uses for multi-currency transfers across 50+ countries.

episodes.title: API Gateway Explained (ByteByteGo)
episodes.description: What an API gateway does: authentication, rate limiting, request routing, protocol translation, and service discovery. How it fits into a microservices architecture.

episodes.title: How a URL Shortener Works — System Design Walkthrough (ByteByteGo)
episodes.description: End-to-end system design for a URL shortener: hash functions, base62 encoding, database schema, caching strategy, and scaling to millions of URLs.

episodes.title: Rate Limiter Design — Token Bucket & Leaky Bucket (ByteByteGo)
episodes.description: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding window — the four rate limiting algorithms explained. How to scale rate limiters in a distributed system.

episodes.title: CAP Theorem Simplified (ByteByteGo)
episodes.description: Why distributed systems must choose between Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance. Clear explanation with real-world database examples (CP vs AP systems).

episodes.title: Consistent Hashing Explained (ByteByteGo)
episodes.description: Visual explainer on consistent hashing — how distributed systems assign keys to nodes and minimize redistribution when nodes are added or removed. Core concept for sharding and distributed caches.

episodes.title: Message Queues & Event-Driven Architecture — Patterns & Tradeoffs
episodes.description: Chris Patterson (MassTransit creator) on message brokers vs event streaming, sagas vs routing slips, transactional outbox pattern, dead-letter queues. Transport-agnostic architectural patterns for distributed systems.

episodes.title: Rate Limiting & High-Traffic Systems — Real Incident Walkthrough
episodes.description: Mojtaba Sarooghi (Queue-it) on handling flash traffic: 100K to 100M requests in one minute, cold-start failures, DynamoDB at 200K TPS, rate limiting algorithms, and bot detection (98% of traffic is bots during ticket drops).

episodes.title: Event Sourcing & CQRS — Architecture Deep Dive
episodes.description: Martin Dilger (author of Understanding Event Sourcing) explains event stores, projections, CQRS, event versioning, and why Kafka is NOT an event store. Practical adoption strategy: 2-day modeling workshop + 1-day build.

episodes.title: System Design Interviews — The Complete Framework
episodes.description: Sriram Panyam (ex-Google, ex-LinkedIn) breaks down the system design interview: 5-phase approach, 25 canonical problems, what interviewers look for at each level, and the key mindset shift from buzzword-driven to requirement-driven design. The single best SDI resource.

episodes.title: That said... — Three Ways to Say I Don't Know
episodes.description: Welcome to Daily Interview English. Episode 4, July 05, 2026.  Today's pattern: "That said..."  Introduces a counterpoint or qualification. episodes.title: What clicked for me was... — 4-Second Pause Protocol
episodes.description: Welcome to Daily Interview English. Episode 2, July 05, 2026.  Today's episode draws from Changelog: "From open source hits to OpenAI (Interview)".  Today's pattern: "What clicked for me was..."  Use this to explain a key realization or motivation. It's more natural than 'I realized' and signals genuine insight.  Here are three examples. Repeat each one out loud after me.  Example 1. What clicked for me was realizing that coding agents let me build software tailored to a team's exact workflow.
